questions.explain: Ingestion is asynchronous and idempotent; retrieval is synchronous and latency-sensitive; SQL Server is the only shared state — workers and API coordinate through tables and queues, never direct calls.
options: Ingestion is synchronous and retrieval is asynchronous
Async idempotent ingestion plus sync latency-sensitive retrieval, with SQL Server as the only shared state
Both halves run in the same process
Ingestion uses Redis and retrieval uses SQL Server
questions.q: How does the end-to-end RAG pipeline split work?

questions.explain: Workers claim rows with READPAST + UPDLOCK (never blocking on another worker's row), and the OR clause reclaims work from dead workers after 15 minutes via the heartbeat timestamp.
options: A Redis queue with blocking pops
One worker per document, manually assigned
Workers poll with NOLOCK
Claim-based queue with READPAST + UPDLOCK and 15-minute reclaim of dead workers' claims
questions.q: How does the claim-based ingest work queue handle crashed workers?

questions.explain: Production retrieval adds query rewriting (cheap model → standalone query), similarity floors with a grounded true/false flag, and citation verification that every cited chunk_id was actually retrieved.
options: Query rewriting, similarity floors with grounded flags, and citation verification
Bigger embedding models only
More API servers
Disabling the full-text arm
questions.q: What three production additions sit on top of the hybrid search core?

questions.explain: The four failure modes: retrieved-but-ignored (context present, model ignores it), chunking damage (answer split across chunks), stale index (old chunks rank after update), and embedding model drift (provider updates model behind the name).
options: Network failures, disk failures, CPU failures, memory failures
Retrieved-but-ignored, chunking damage, stale index, embedding model drift
Only hallucinations
Only rate limiting
questions.q: What are the four RAG failure modes and their character?

questions.explain: A citation to a chunk that was never retrieved is a hallucinated citation — worse than no citation — so every cited chunk_id must mechanically verify against the retrieved set for that turn.
options: Citations are optional decoration
Every cited chunk_id must be in the retrieved set; a hallucinated citation is worse than none
The model can cite any document it knows
Citations are only for compliance reviewers
questions.q: Why must citations be mechanically verified?

title: Building End-to-End RAG on SQL Server
